Because of the limitations of web browser technology, copying and pasting text in Microsoft 365 for the web differs from copying and pasting text in the Office desktop applications. This article gives you steps for copying and pasting in each of the Microsoft 365 for the web programs.

section: Word for the web > Viewing in browser (Reading mode)
text: To select individual words or phrases, or to paste content into the document, click Edit in browser.

section: Word for the web > Viewing in browser (Reading mode)
text: If you want to paste within the document, click Edit in Browser.

section: Word for the web > Reviewing or editing in browser
text: When the document is in Editing or Reviewing mode, you can work with content much like you do in the Word desktop app. Press Ctrl+C to copy, Ctrl+X to cut, or Ctrl+V to paste the text or picture (Windows); or press ⌘+C, ⌘+X, or ⌘+V (Mac). On Chrome, Firefox, and Chromium-based Microsoft Edge, you can also use Ctrl+Shift+V and ⌘+Shift+V to paste text only (pastes text without source formatting).

section: Word for the web > Reviewing or editing in browser
text: If you're using Firefox and you want to use the Copy, Cut, and Paste commands on the Word for the web ribbon, you need to allow JavaScript to use the clipboard. If you don't want to do this, use the -C, -X, and -V keyboard commands.

section: Word for the web > Reviewing or editing in browser
text: On Chrome, you can install the Office - Enable Copy and Paste Extension, which will allow you to cut, copy, and paste with your mouse on all the Office Online apps.

section: Word for the web > Pasting from outside Word for the web
text: When you paste text from outside Word for the web, you have two options for how to paste the text: keep source formatting and paste text only. For the default paste (keep source), the text is inserted into the document with as many of the original formatting properties that can be copied. Characteristics of the text, such as bold, italics, or a particular size or color, are preserved whenever possible. Depending on the source of your copied content, specific formatting aspects might not paste as expected. In this case, you can use the formatting tools in Word for the web to reapply these formatting properties.

section: Word for the web > Pasting from outside Word for the web
text: For paste text only, the text and words are preserved, but the formatting will match the line of your document where you paste the content. Paste text only can be accessed via the ribbon and context menu (when you're using any version of Microsoft Edge, or Chrome with the Office - Enable Copy and Paste Extension), via Ctrl+Shift+V (Chrome, Firefox, and Chromium-based Microsoft Edge), or by clicking the paste floatie after standard paste and selecting the "paste text only" option.
